sources.claim: Recombinant IDOLDH reduced ipsdienone to the minus alcohol; plus products were not observed in the reported assays.
The named alcohol substrate is R-ipsdienol; both NAD and NADP are represented in the reaction nomenclature.

reviews.reason: The measured product stereoselectivity and official R-substrate assignment do not support production of the exact S target.
reviews.scope_limit: Does not prove that no other enzyme or engineered variant can make the S product. No Cannabis protein activity is established.
reviews.next_test: Find and assay an S-product-selective reductase; distinguish product enantiomers and test exact cofactor preference.

reviews.required_direction: exact camphor reduction to the encoded isoborneol stereoisomer

sources.claim: Recombinant sage enzymes preferentially oxidized racemic borneol to plus camphor and racemic isoborneol to minus camphor.
An engineered Arabidopsis lyrata AlBDH L205F variant reduced plus camphor to plus borneol and minus camphor to plus isoborneol.

reviews.reason: The retrieved sage abstract concerns oxidation, while the AlBDH abstract names different stereoisomeric reduction products. Neither is an exact substrate-product-direction assignment for this proposed step.
reviews.scope_limit: Abstract-level review is not an exhaustive enzyme search. Full-text stereochemical assignments, cofactor specificity and exact chemical joins remain to be verified. No Cannabis activity is established.
reviews.next_test: Seek an exact camphor/isoborneol stereochemical product assignment in a reduction assay before choosing a genome-search reference.

claim_boundary: Negative assignment decisions are specific to the reviewed evidence, not proof of biological impossibility. Existing structural hypotheses and their conditional certificates are unchanged; zero supported-reaction or pathway-coverage gain is claimed. Optical rotation is never calculated from an R/S label; literature rotation assignments and encoded absolute stereochemistry remain distinct evidence.
